question: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of severe abdominal pain for the past 2 hours. He has a 2-year history of burning epigastric pain that gets worse with meals. His pulse is 120/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 60/40 mm Hg. Despite appropriate lifesaving measures, he dies. At autopsy, examination shows erosion of the right gastric artery. Perforation of an ulcer in which of the following locations most likely caused this patient's findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Peptic ulcer in the anterior duodenum -> erosion of the right gastric artery -> severe abdominal pain -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Perforation of an ulcer in the posterior duodenum -> erosion of the right gastric artery -> severe abdominal pain -> 75% confidence. CHAIN: Perforation of an ulcer in the lesser curvature of the stomach -> erosion of the right gastric artery -> severe abdominal pain -> 80%
analysis: The erosion of the right gastric artery suggests a gastric ulcer complication. Given the patient's history of burning epigastric pain that worsens with meals, the most likely location for the ulcer leading to the erosion of the right gastric artery is the lesser curvature of the stomach.
